intro: Look at that great limestone outcrop rising from the middle of the Cilician plain. This is Anavarza, ancient Anazarbus, in Adana province. Its story runs from the 1st century BC to the 14th century AD. A Roman city famous for its monumental triumphal arch and its fortress — let us explore it together.
history: Rome brought the city under its control in the 1st century BC, and under Septimius Severus it gained the proud title of metropolis. The centuries that followed saw Byzantine, Arab, Armenian and Mamluk periods, and people kept on living here through all of them. So how did it end? After the Mamluks took the city in 1375, it was abandoned.
structure-1: You are now in front of the Triumphal Arch, known as Alakapı. This is Anavarza's Roman triumphal arch, with three arches. Stand beneath it for a moment and imagine processions passing through.
structure-5: Now lift your eyes to Anavarza Castle. The medieval castle sits on the rock, keeping watch over the Roman city below.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Colonnaded Street, the Theatre and the Stadium.
facts: Did you know? Anavarza is known as the birthplace of the famous physician Dioscorides, author of De Materia Medica — for centuries Europe's standard pharmacology text. Excavations since 2013 have revealed the world's first known double-lane colonnaded road. The city sits at the foot of a vast sheer rock, with the castle on top and the city on the plain. Its colonnaded street and triumphal arch survive, and the mosaics from its villas are among the finest in the region.
outro: This brings our tour of Anavarza, ancient Anazarbus, to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for your company, and enjoy your visit.
